title: Differential Item Functioning for Annotator-Group Bias in Preference Data

original_idea.body:
# DIF for Annotator-Group Bias in Preference Data

**Problem:** Aggregated preference labels may hide group-dependent value conflicts (DIF).

**Direction:** Apply DIF to preference items using group metadata or persona-prompted judges; map high-DIF content areas.

**Why it matters:** Surfaces where alignment encodes one group's values.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2404.10271; arXiv:2404.13038; arXiv:2503.10229.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Pluralistic-alignment fairness is recognized but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: DIF statistics plus persona-prompted groups; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused DIF-mapping; needs group-labeled or simulated data.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open data, persona prompting; lab-independent fairness auditing.

low_compute.reasoning: Mostly inference and statistics; one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: DIF applied to preference items appears mostly unexplored though related fairness work exists.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: DIF on preference items may be open; related fairness work exists.
